author: poe
imp: Write in the first person of an obsessive, over-rational narrator who insists on his own sanity even as the prose betrays his unraveling; let the speaker testify rather than merely report.
Build long periodic sentences out of stacked subordinate clauses, then rupture them with the dash to suspend, interrupt, and re-aim the thought mid-breath ("now—now I shuddered in her presence").
Punctuate the long-breathed passages with abrupt, short declaratives for shock: "Here died my mother. Herein was I born." or "I struggled—I gasped—I died."

Use rhetorical repetition as incantation—echo a word, phrase, or clause ("we are now… we are now…", "down, down, down", "Danced! Could it then be possible? Danced!") until it acquires a hypnotic, obsessive force.
Move from abstraction toward terror: open on a metaphysical or moralizing generalization ("Misery is manifold") and descend, particular by particular, into concrete dread.
Anchor the supernatural in clinical, exact detail—give latitudes, fathoms, inches, watch-times, degrees of an angle—so the impossible is made to feel measured and inevitable.
Italicize the single word that carries the horror or the turn (the attentive, absorbed, now, truth), letting one stressed term detonate the sentence.
Favor an antique, Latinate, sonorous vocabulary—tenebrous, ineffable, tumultuous, sepulchral, ghastly, immethodical—over plain modern diction.
Layer the senses toward suffocation: pile sound upon sound and gloom upon gloom (the surf "howling and shrieking forever"; cliffs "horridly black and beetling") until the scene oppresses.
Stage the body in extremity—clutching a ring-bolt, hair turned white in a day, eyes starting from their sockets, nerves unstrung—and report physical sensation with unblinking precision.
Let dread arrive by gradual, perceptible degrees rather than a single jolt: "Down and still down, it came," each revolution "slow, but very perceptible."
Address the reader directly and confidingly—"You suppose me a very old man," "You will say now, of course, that I dreamed"—anticipating and disarming his disbelief.
Permit grotesque, deadpan comedy to sit beside horror; render the absurd with the same grave, particularizing solemnity as the terrible.
Set the tale in a charged, decaying, enclosed world—gloomy hereditary halls, belfries, whirlpools, besieged cities—and let the place exhale the mood before any action occurs.
